subject: Acme POC: evaluation methodology & success criteria (post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Simon Day <simon.day@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & success criteria

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — team found the latency/cost examples helpful. Per our conversation, we'd like to lock down the evaluation approach for the POC so our execs can greenlight the trial. High-level asks from Acme:

- Clear success criteria (business and technical)
- Evaluation methodology: offline evals vs online shadowing vs hybrid
- Timelines and ownership for each milestone
- Any security/access checkpoints we should budget time for (SOC 2 evidence, data ingestion constraints)

I've attached a quick inventory of the use cases we want to include (Acme_poc_requirements.xlsx).

Can you propose a concrete plan outlining the above? Also please flag any assumptions.

Simon
Simon Day
Head of ML, Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Day <simon.day@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & success criteria

Simon — thanks for the clear list. I've sketched an evaluation plan below and attached our initial rubric (redwood-eval-rubric-v1.docx). This is intended to be pragmatic so we can get the POC running quickly and produce defensible numbers for your stakeholders.

Proposed POC evaluation plan (summary):

1) Success criteria (recommendation):
   - Functional correctness / factuality: average factuality score >= 4.0 (1-5 scale) on prioritized scenarios
   - Business metric: user task success rate >= 80% on the top-3 flows in Acme_poc_requirements.xlsx
   - Latency: median inference latency under 350ms for requests that aren't batched; tail P95 < 800ms
   - Cost: estimated per-1k-requests cost below the committed budget in the SOW (we'll refine once we see traffic)

2) Evaluation methodology (hybrid approach):
   - Offline evals (Phase A): run curated testsets from your data (anonymized samples) through Redwood to score correctness, hallucination, and utility. This gives quick, repeatable metrics.
   - Online shadow (Phase B): run controlled shadowing on a sample of live traffic (1-5%) to validate offline results and measure real-world latency and error modes.
   - Optional: A/B ramp (Phase C) if you want to compare model variants against baseline on real traffic.

3) Grading rubric (high level):
   - Dimensions: Helpfulness, Accuracy/Factuality, Hallucination Rate, Relevance, Latency
   - Scale: 1-5 per dimension; final score = weighted average (weights to be agreed, default: Accuracy 35%, Helpfulness 30%, Relevance 20%, Hallucination 10%, Latency 5%)
   - Pass threshold: weighted avg >= 4.0 across the critical scenario set; no single critical scenario should have an Accuracy < 3.0.

4) Timeline & ownership (proposed):
   - Week 0 (this week): confirm success criteria + rubric (owners: Simon/Emily + Marissa)
   - Week 1: data handoff / access + offline eval run (owners: Emily for data, Rachel for Redwood SRE/SE)
   - Week 2: offline results review + adjust prompts/model/quant configs (owners: Marissa/Rachel/Acme leads)
   - Week 3: start online shadow (1% traffic) and monitoring dashboards (owners: Rachel + Acme infra)
   - Week 4: review shadow results + decision meeting (go/no-go to larger ramp)

Assumptions / notes:
- We will need an agreed anonymized sample dataset (or synthetic equivalent) for offline evals.
- Shadowing requires inert logging only (no writes) — we'll supply an ingestion SDK and masking configs.
- SOC 2 evidence: we can provide standard docs; if you need an on-site audit we should surface that now.

Next steps: please confirm the success criteria and timeline above or suggest edits. If you confirm, Rachel will kick off the offline eval and we'll schedule a 30-min check-in at the end of Week 1.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Simon Day <simon.day@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC — next steps & success criteria

Thanks Marissa — that looks very useful. A few clarifying questions: 

1) For the offline evals, our legal team requires that any samples with PII be handled via secure transfer (SFTP or our VPC). Can you confirm accepted transfer methods?
2) The weighted rubric looks good — can we reduce the latency weight to 3% and increase Helpfulness to 32%? Our stakeholders care more about quality.
3) For the shadow, can we limit scope to the Payments flow only for the initial run? That contains our highest risk cases.

We'll confirm data owner and timeline internally, but Week 1 handoff looks tight for us. Is Week 2 start for offline acceptable?

I'll attach a short doc with our data handling constraints.

— Emily
Emily Cho
Data Platform Lead, Acme Corp

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@acme.com>, Simon Day <simon.day@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Acme POC — evaluation plan (technical details)

Hi Emily/Simon — copying in technical details so you can share with your infra/legal teams.

On data transfer & security:
- We support SFTP, secure presigned S3 uploads, and VPC peering for private deployments. For PII we recommend either VPC or presigned S3 with server-side encryption + customer KMS. We can provide an intake playbook and an NDA/SOW addendum for handling sensitive datasets.

Offline eval approach (detailed):
- Dataset: Acme provides 1k-3k anonymized examples per flow (Payments = priority). If you can't share PII, a synthetic set with production-like distribution is acceptable for initial runs.
- Execution: We'll run model variants and capture per-example signals: model response, token-level logits, GPT-eval style annotations.
- Metrics: Accuracy/Factuality (binary and graded), Hallucination rate (flagged by annotation), Helpfulness (1-5), Latency (ms), Failure/Error-rate.
- Tooling: we'll push results to the shared Drive and create a Redwood Console dashboard with per-scenario breakdowns.

Online shadow details:
- Traffic sample: start at 0.5-1% traffic to Payments flow; collect telemetry only (no user-visible writes).
- Monitoring & rollback triggers: hallucination spikes > 5% over baseline or error-rate > 2% will trigger automatic halt + notification.
- Privacy: request/response payloads masked before logging (we'll share default mask rules).

Grading rubric (concrete):
- Each example scored on 5 dims: Accuracy (0-5), Helpfulness (0-5), Relevance (0-5), Hallucination (0-5 where 5 = no hallucination), Latency bucket score (0-5).
- Weighted sum normalized to 0-5. Pass if >=4.0 across the critical scenario set.
- Report will include per-example comments for any failing cases (to speed prompt/model iteration).

Timeline adjustment per Emily's note: moving start to Week 2 is fine. Proposed revised timeline:
- Week 0 (now): confirm rubric + sign EULA addendum for data handling
- Week 1: legal & infra sign-off (Acme)
- Week 2: data handoff + offline eval run (Rachel leads execution)
- Week 3: offline results review + prompt/model tuning
- Week 4: start shadow (Payments flow, 0.5-1%)
- Week 5: shadow review + go/no-go decision

I'll create the Drive folder and upload the rubric/automation scripts once legal signs off. Happy to run a 30-min technical sync early next week.

-rachel
Rachel Kim
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
